chunk-001:c004.proposition: Evidence of intelligent design or an expressed peaceful intention does not securely identify a benevolent source, since a deceptive agent could produce the same apparent signs.

orphanFallback.rationale: Malpass's signal and biblical-sign analogies independently establish a gap between detecting intentional agency and inferring that the agent is good, so the proposition can introduce the divine-psychology objection without an earlier opposing move.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Advanced aliens, future time travelers, and simulators form a disjunctive naturalistic alternative whose combined probability must be compared with theism.

orphanFallback.rationale: Malpass expressly supplies three naturalistic explanations and directs that their probabilities be combined, which independently states the relevant comparison class without requiring a prior opposing move.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: A consequential fine-tuning argument must specify its theistic hypothesis and show that it explains the evidence better than every admissible naturalistic version, not merely one selected rival.

orphanFallback.rationale: Malpass independently distinguishes the trivial comparison of some theism with some naturalism from the stronger universal comparison, supplying a standalone burden for evaluating the inference.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: General theism predicts a particular resurrection no better than general alienism because both posit powerful agents whose intentions remain largely unknown.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source directly compares two agent hypotheses and observes that neither its power nor its general description entails the specific event, making this a self-contained illustration of empirical underdetermination.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Broad naturalistic simulation and science-fiction possibilities can accommodate nearly any observation, preventing such evidence from decisively separating naturalism from theism.

orphanFallback.rationale: Malpass explicitly argues that naturalistic scenarios remain compatible with almost any proposed observation, so the proposition independently advances persistent empirical ambiguity without relying on a prior selected challenge.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: The disjunction of every specifically limited alternative may have greater total prior probability than a single unlimited hypothesis, reversing the alleged simplicity advantage of the unlimited hypothesis.

orphanFallback.rationale: Malpass's aggregation argument directly contrasts one unlimited hypothesis with the summed probability of all limited hypotheses, so it stands alone as a prior-probability objection.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Naturalism's ontological economy may offset theism's advantages in coherence or modesty because theism adds supernatural commitments to the natural reality it also posits.

orphanFallback.rationale: Malpass independently identifies ontological parsimony as a competing theoretical virtue and grounds it in theism's additional supernatural commitments, making the point constructive without an earlier opposing move.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Apparent fine-tuning may be a property indicating a defect in the operative physical theory rather than an objective feature of the universe that requires a design explanation.

orphanFallback.rationale: Malpass reports the physicists' theory-level interpretation of fine-tuning and its implication that severe tuning counts against the theory, providing a standalone challenge to the datum's explanatory status.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: Fine-tuning cannot reliably favor theism when divine goodness, values, reasons, and resulting choices are too uncertain to ground a determinate likelihood for a life-permitting universe.

orphanFallback.rationale: Malpass directly traces uncertainty from whether God is good through what divine goodness means to what such a being would choose, independently establishing the missing predictive bridge.
